en.name: Saint Mark, Evangelist
en.summary: Honors the author of the earliest Gospel and the traditional founder of the Church in Alexandria.
en.body: This feast honors Mark, companion of Peter and Paul and, by strong early tradition, the author of the earliest of the four Gospels, a fast-paced and vivid account believed to draw heavily on Peter's own preaching and recollections in Rome. Tradition holds he later founded the Church in Alexandria, Egypt, one of the most significant sees of the early Christian world, and was martyred there. His relics were later brought to Venice, where he became the city's patron, his emblem of a winged lion becoming a defining symbol of Venetian identity still visible across the city today, including atop columns in St. Mark's Square and on the facade of the basilica that bears his name.
